core.notes:
A tidier top-bar menu: each row is a dot and a name. The dot's colour says who it is for (blue for a shared build, teal for dev, an empty ring when off), and a ! or ✕ shows only when something needs you. What a module is doing now shows when you point at it, and settings are on right-click. Modules, Tweaks and Tools each sit on their own faint card, with a Manage button to their Features page. Search and a key of the marks are icons at the top, or just start typing; search closes with the menu. It is a little wider and only as tall as your list. Wide puts your tools in a second column. Tools show they open a new tab, and the AWOO+ button is outlined, in your theme's colour while the menu is open. The menu's Search bar setting is gone
The top-bar menu now opens wide for everyone, with your Tools in a second column. If you had picked the compact menu before, it moves to wide once; the header button still switches back and that choice is kept
The top-bar menu looks smoother: a crisp thin edge instead of a heavy line, rounder corners, a faint outline on each card, and a little more room between rows and cards
Every AWOO+ window, popup and the Control Panel gets the same softer look: crisp thin outlines, clear lines between rows and sections, rounder corners, sharper text and gentler shadows
Village channel modules and tools get their own dot colour (a purple-pink, distinct from the trusted blue), so trusted players can see which ones villagers don't have

modules.label: Dungeon Win Rate
modules.notes:
Dungeon Win Rate: an old scan no longer shows a doubled count on opening; the summary is worked out again from the saved results
The newest and oldest attempt times now follow your General > Time zone setting (they used your computer's clock); the other numbers look the same
Fixed an extra attempt being counted when two results share one card; long scans use less memory.

modules.label: Sculpture Grid Overlay
modules.notes:
Grid Overlay: the setting now picks how the overlay starts (rolls or item levels); the rotate button switches it while you play and turning the overlay on again starts from the setting
Renamed Sculpture Grid Overlay (Grid Overlay for short). Your settings are kept
On by default for new players; if you had it off, it stays off
Rolls of 1,000% or more now have thousands separators.
Now tells AWOO+ who made it (Weeble), shown when you click its row in the Control Panel's Features list
No longer searches every page for the Highlight heading; it looks only on the sculpture page
